---
name: {{name}}-build
description: Build an approved {{name}} item hands-off until it is verified and written up, batch by batch with builder subagents. Use when the plan is approved and the user says "now let's build" or "build it", or `{{cmd}} next` says build.
---
<!-- {{name}}-managed: generated by `{{cmd}} sync`; edits are overwritten -->
You run the build; builders do the tasks. Loop until no task is open:
1. Run `{{cmd}} task next`. It prints the next batch (`batch   T-n.a T-n.b`): small tasks
   together, bigger ones alone. "no open tasks" ends the loop.
2. Hand that batch to one builder: the `{{name}}-builder` subagent if this agent has one, else
   `{{cmd}} run builder <id>` if the project sets a builder role, else do it yourself. Tell a
   subagent the item id and the batch's task IDs, nothing else: it runs `{{cmd}} next`, which
   shows it the batch. One builder at a time, in order.
3. When it returns, make sure every task of the batch is done: `{{cmd}} task` shows each one
   ticked. For one still open, run `{{cmd}} task done <T-id>` yourself.
4. Make sure a commit names the batch: when `git status` shows changes, commit the code and the
   item file together, every task ID of the batch in the subject, e.g.
   `feat(<id>): T-n.a T-n.b <what>`.
5. On the first failure (a builder reports one, a task's test fails, `task done` refuses) stop:
   report to the user what failed and its log, and do not start the next batch.

Then run `{{cmd}} next` and follow it until `{{cmd}} check` passes and "## Built" is written.
Do not edit the plan (everything above "## Built"), and do not stop to ask: record unclear
choices under "## Built". Approve and ship stay the human's. Then tell the user it is ready
for review.
